purpose: Seeds and assumptions for the linked-account review study (B6). Synthetic pseudonymous accounts only (ids like a0001); no real wallets, devices, residences or routes.

reviewer.note: carried over from the #123 study as an assumption; not measured

staffMinutes.note: ASSUMPTIONS; no measured reviewer time exists

hypotheses_stated_before_results: F1 The #123 headline 1.3% is a wrongly-upheld rate; the share of honest accounts that are put into a review under the 4-of-14 rule is several times larger (expect >= 10% of accounts in linked-family cohorts).
F2 Cohorts with no link edges between strangers (commuters, night shift, parks, transit, drift) stay below 1% reviewed under every link-based variant, because proximity alone is never used.
F3 Rings whose accounts are not linked are detected at ~0% by every variant; staggered-start rings evade all variants.
F4 Requiring a tight-trace feature lowers family review rates, but a ring that spaces its phones evades it.
F5 A naive proximity-only counterfactual would put a double-digit share of commuters and park walkers into review, which is why proximity alone is not evidence.

Pass bar for a recommendable review rule (stated now): honest-cohort review rate <= 2% overall at N=1000, no cohort of strangers above 1%, linked-ring detection >= 80%. Failing any is reported as failing.
